# Codex Instructions

## Beads Issue Tracker

Use Beads (`bd`) for durable task tracking in repositories that include it. Use the `beads` skill at `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` (project install) or `~/.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` (global install) for Beads workflow guidance, then use the `bd` CLI for issue operations.

### Quick Reference

```bash
bd ready                # Find available work
bd show <id>            # View issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim work
bd close <id>           # Complete work
bd prime                # Refresh Beads context
```

### Rules

- Use `bd` for all task tracking; do not create markdown TODO lists.
- Run `bd prime` when Beads context is missing or stale. Codex 0.129.0+ can load Beads context automatically through native hooks; use `/hooks` to inspect or toggle them.
- Keep persistent project memory in Beads via `bd remember`; do not create ad hoc memory files.

**Architecture in one line:** issues live in a local Dolt DB; sync uses `refs/dolt/data` on your git remote; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a passive export. See https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/docs/core-concepts/sync-concepts.md for details and anti-patterns.

## Autonomous backend workflow

These rules govern the workflow, including guidance emitted by Beads and Ralph.
The user authorizes implementation, tests, commits, and YouGile task transitions.

- YouGile project `umirHack-flagman`, board `dev`, is the source of requirements.
  Select backend stories from `To do(backend)` by ascending S number, starting
  with S08. Do not touch S07: another agent owns it.
- Read the full story and all its subtasks. Mirror them in Beads with the
  YouGile IDs. Use `bd --sandbox` for every issue operation; never sync or push.
- Claim one story, move it to `In progress`, and implement its subtasks in order.
  Subtasks without columns remain subtasks; do not create duplicate board cards.
- Use Serena for symbol navigation. Preserve architecture and unrelated changes.
- Complete one story per iteration. Add meaningful tests, run gofmt, then run
  `go -C backend test ./...`, `go -C backend vet ./...`, and
  `go -C backend build ./...`. PostgreSQL integration tests must also pass for
  changes involving queries; use a dedicated local test database.
- Create ONE conventional Git commit for the completed story and its subtasks.
  Stage explicit related paths. Use the existing repository author and committer.
  Do not change identity, add AI attribution or co-author trailers, amend, rebase,
  push, merge into dev/main/master, or modify main/master. Work on `agent/s08`
  in `/home/sklyarvlad/work/umirHack-flagman`, the user's main project directory.
  A fast-forward to finished prerequisites before a new story is allowed.
- Assign the user Vladislav (`sklyarvladislavtl@gmail.com`) to the story and
  every subtask in YouGile. Mark each subtask complete in YouGile and Beads
  immediately after its implementation and relevant verification succeed.
- Only after final verification and the story commit, close the story in Beads,
  mark it complete in YouGile, and move it to `Done`.
- Then import and claim the next ready backend story. Never close failing work.
  Record blockers in Beads and leave unfinished YouGile cards in `In progress`.
- Never access production, commit secrets, run destructive migrations, modify
  unrelated files, spawn agents, or disable the Codex OS sandbox.
- Keep tokens outside the repository. Do not print authorization headers.
- Never track or commit `.serena/`, `.beads/`, or `.beads.gate.lock`.
- Make routine implementation decisions autonomously without user questions.
- Use `./scripts/yougile-queue.sh subtask <bd-id>` after a subtask is implemented;
  it verifies backend and marks that subtask complete in both systems.
- Include the story number (for example S09) in the conventional commit subject.
  Commit messages must contain no references to agents, neural networks, AI tools,
  or generated code. Use neutral scopes such as menu, orders, workflow, git or docs.
  After committing, call `./scripts/yougile-queue.sh finish <bd-story-id>`;
  it verifies the commit, closes the story, moves it to Done, and claims the next.
- New integration tests should use `FLAGMAN_TEST_DATABASE_URL` or the appropriate
  named test URL inherited by the launcher. Never use the application's database.
- The quota guard pauses the workflow when the five-hour or weekly Codex quota
  has at most 5% remaining. Preserve unfinished code and Beads status. On restart,
  inspect the working tree and the current story; repeat verification before closing.
  During a pause, active stories and subtasks become `blocked` with a
  `workflow_pause` marker and a recorded reason. After a successful quota check,
  the launcher restores only its own paused tasks to `in_progress`. Keep other
  blockers intact. YouGile's unfinished story stays in `In progress`.
  Resume existing `in_progress` subtasks before claiming new ready work.

Beads uses this repository's local `.beads` database. The local Ralph
compatibility overrides make Ralph use the same database instead of an
obsolete separate SQLite store.
